title: Design-Modulus Duality for Minimax Treated Quantile Estimation with Known Propensity
banked_reason: Cold D0.5.G verdict: tier=subfield, novelty floor=field, paper_score_ceiling=7.2 < ceiling_for_field=7.4, salvageable=false.
gap_reasons: The result is nevertheless confined to a scalar uniform covariate, exactly known propensity, bounded outcomes, and thresholdwise Lipschitz conditional CDFs, while the Avella-Medina–Davis–Samorodnitsky bridge covers only a specially constructed constant-bounded subclass.

The certification theorem establishes eventual termination but supplies neither a complexity bound nor an implemented design analysis, so the claimed practical computability has no delivered performance evidence.
The NSW–PSID discussion remains motivation rather than an application, limiting the significance and reproducibility case for a leading econometrics journal despite the complete theoretical bracket.

The closest limited-overlap comparator, Ma--Huang--Namkoong (arXiv:2511.22003), is described only as trimming-bias sensitivity although it also uses known propensities and a finite-sample Lipschitz minimax estimator/CI framework for ATEs; add a theorem-level comparison stating the exact target, experiment, and optimality differences (and position the related limited-overlap ATE-CI class) before claiming this frontier is unoccupied.

tldr: For a known one-dimensional propensity, attainable precision for a marginal treated quantile is characterized by the entire supplied design through a positive Wasserstein-bias plus inverse-design-standard-deviation program and its Lipschitz testing dual. A proper monotone weighted CDF and bias-aware interval attain the program, while bounded common-support observed-law pairs give matching root-MSE and honest-length converses. Strict overlap is root-\(n\), quadratic contact gives \(n^{-2/5}\), and critical linear contact gives \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\). At \(e(x)=x/2\), the explicit lower pair satisfies the regular variation, conditional-law convergence, and local anti-concentration hypotheses of Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky with \(\gamma_1=2\); an explicit clipped positive CDF also gives matching uniform risk and honest-length upper bounds on a constant-bounded version of that class. The comparison with \(e(x)=x^2/2\) establishes insufficiency of the shared coarse square-root envelope, not insufficiency of the exact regular-variation index, because the two designs have \(\gamma_1=2\) and \(\gamma_1=3/2\), respectively.
gap: Published weak-overlap quantile work derives truncated-IPW limit laws under regular variation, while optimal-recovery work treats causal means or linear functionals and trimming-sensitivity work diagnoses extrapolation bias. These literatures do not characterize minimax marginal-quantile risk and honest expected interval length for every supplied propensity by one evaluable object, nor do they show that two designs under one tail envelope can have different recovery orders.
fill: The project derives a positive primal and Lipschitz dual, proves same-design upper and lower statistical bounds after quantile inversion, exhibits a same-envelope pair with different recovery orders, evaluates further geometries, and develops its own cell-treatment-mass reduction with a zero-safe continuum lift.
